title: The Real Christmas Story and the Temple Flex
paragraphs: §The Birth of Jesus

Around that time, the Roman Emperor, Caesar Augustus, flexed his power and ordered a massive census across the entire empire. (This was the first census, back when Quirinius was governor of Syria.) Everyone had to travel back to their ancestral hometown to register. Because Joseph was a descendant of King David, he packed up a very pregnant Mary — his fiancée — and hiked from Nazareth all the way to Bethlehem, David's town.

While they were there, the time came for Mary to give birth. She had her firstborn son, wrapped him tightly in strips of cloth, and laid him in a manger — because there was no room for them in the inn.
§An Event for Everyone

That same night, there were some tough shepherds out in the fields keeping night watch over their sheep. Suddenly, an angel of the Lord appeared right in front of them, and the blinding glory of God lit up the entire field. The shepherds were absolutely terrified.

"Don't panic! I am bringing you massive good news that will bring ultimate joy to all people. Today in the town of David, a Savior has been born to you; he is the Messiah, the Lord. Here is how you'll know it's him: you will find a baby wrapped tightly in cloth, lying in a manger."
Suddenly, a massive army of angels appeared in the sky, shouting and praising God: "Glory to God in the highest heaven, and peace on earth to the people he favors!"

When the angels left, the shepherds looked at each other and said, "Let's go to Bethlehem right now and see this!" They sprinted to the town, found Mary, Joseph, and the baby in the manger. Seeing was believing — they told everyone they met what the angels had said about this child, and everyone who heard was impressed.

Mary kept all these things to herself, holding them dear, deep within herself. The shepherds went back home, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen — it had turned out exactly the way they'd been told!
§Blessings
Eight days later, they circumcised the baby and officially named him Jesus — the exact name the angel had given before he was even conceived.

When the days for Mary's purification under Moses' law were complete, they took baby Jesus up to Jerusalem to present him to God, exactly as the law commanded: "Every firstborn son belongs to the Lord." They also offered the sacrifice the law prescribed: a pair of doves.

There was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon — a good man who lived in prayerful expectancy, waiting for God to rescue Israel. The Holy Spirit was on him, and the Spirit had shown him he would see God's Messiah before he died. Led by the Spirit, Simeon walked into the Temple at the exact moment Mary and Joseph arrived with baby Jesus to do what the law required. He scooped the baby into his arms and blessed God: "Lord, you can let me die in peace now, because my eyes have seen your salvation — out in the open for everyone to see: a light revealing you to the non-Jewish nations, and glory for your people Israel!"

Jesus' father and mother were speechless with surprise at these words. Then Simeon blessed them and said to Mary: "This child will cause many in Israel to fall and many to rise — a figure misunderstood and contradicted. And a sword will pierce your own heart too. But this rejection will force honesty, as God reveals who people really are."

Anna the prophetess was also there — a daughter of Phanuel from the tribe of Asher, a very old woman by now. She had been married seven years and a widow for eighty-four. She never left the Temple area, worshiping night and day with fasting and prayer. At the very moment Simeon was praying, she showed up, broke into praise to God, and talked about the child to everyone waiting expectantly for Jerusalem's rescue.
When they finished everything required by God's Law, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth. There the child grew strong in body and wise in spirit, and the grace of God was on him.
§They Found Him in the Temple

Every year, Jesus' parents traveled to Jerusalem for the massive Passover festival. When he was twelve, they went up as they always did. When the festival ended and they left for home, the child Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem — but his parents didn't know it. Thinking he was somewhere in the traveling group, they journeyed for a whole day, then started looking for him among relatives and friends. When they didn't find him, they went back to Jerusalem to search.

The next day they found him in the Temple, sitting among the teachers — listening to them and asking questions. The teachers were seriously impressed with the sharpness of his answers. But his parents were not impressed; they were upset and hurt. His mother said, "Young man, why have you done this to us? Your father and I have been half out of our minds looking for you!"
He said, "Why were you looking for me? Didn't you know that I had to be here, dealing with the things of my Father?" But they had no idea what he was talking about.

So he went back to Nazareth with them and lived obediently with them. His mother held all these things dearly, deep within herself. And Jesus matured, growing up in both body and spirit, blessed by both God and people.
